docs.title: Ranks and percentiles
docs.text:
Every rank, percentile and decile reads 1 as the healthiest area, the opposite of SIMD. Ranks are over Great Britain, not Scotland. Editions are not comparable with each other: use one edition per study and never compare editions over time.

Every _rnk column is a rank over Great Britain with 1 the healthiest; every _dec column a decile 1 to 10 with 1 the healthiest. The percentiles come in two scales, as the document below (maintained as docs/PERCENTILES.md in the repository) explains. Decision: percentile-scales; ranks-gb-only.

docs.title: Why indicator percentiles run 0 to 100 and domain percentiles 1 to 100
docs.text:
Observed in every file from version 3 onward: the indicator percentiles (14 indicators in v3 and v4, 15 in v5.1) take 101 distinct values, 0 to 100; the four domain percentiles and the index percentile take 100 values, 1 to 100.

The cause is two formulas in the published build code, https://github.com/GeographicDataService/ahah: ahah/create_index.py for v3 and v4 (v4 commit 722fe5f, lines 62 to 97), and the "Create Index" cell of AHAH_Build_Indicator.ipynb for v5 (commit 6ebb0ae).

# indicators: truncation toward zero, divided by the largest rank
idx[f"{col}_pct"] = (idx[f"{col}_rnk"] / idx[f"{col}_rnk"].max() * 100).astype(int)
# domains and index: a hundred equal bins, labelled 1 to 100
idx[f"domain_{d}_pct"] = pd.qcut(idx[f"domain_{d}_rnk"], 100, labels=False) + 1
idx["ahah_pct"] = pd.qcut(idx["ahah_rnk"], 100, labels=False) + 1

Checked on 29 October 2026 against the published ranks of v3, v4 and v5.1, with zero mismatches:

  • indicator percentile = floor(rank × 100 / max rank). Rank 1 to about 430 become 0, and only the largest rank reaches 100. The divisor is the largest rank, not the number of areas: in v4 the five health indicators are ranked with method="dense", so the largest GP rank is 42,644 in a file of 42,648 areas, and dividing by the number of areas gives 199 wrong cells.
  • domain and index percentile = max(1, ceil((rank − 1) × 100 / (n − 1))), which is what qcut on the ranks produces.

The v5 methodology report, section 7, says indicator percentiles are "(1-100)". The files contradict it. The likely reading is that one scale was intended and the indicator line is a shortcut carried since v3. An issue was logged with the authors on 29 October 2026 (text in ISSUE_DRAFT_percentiles.md). Until they answer, the build takes the files as they are.

Consequences for the build:

  • Store the published values unchanged. The checks accept 0 to 100 for indicator percentiles and 1 to 100 for domain and index percentiles, and fail outside those.
  • The two kinds of percentile are not the same scale. The data dictionary says so on each column.
  • Rank 1 is the best area in every column, so a low percentile is good. SIMD is the opposite: band 1 is most deprived. The README says this once, early.
  • Ranks cannot be recomputed from the published values, which are rounded. The published ranks are the only exact ordering; anyone who wants one consistent scale derives it from them, as a named derived column.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• one-table-all-editions: One table, ahah_datazone, keyed by (ahah_version, datazone_code), one row per Scottish data zone per edition, with datazone_vintage. All five editions (1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1) are carried.
  • v5-1-names: Column names are those of the version 5.1 file. Earlier editions map onto them by an explicit per-edition mapping (mapping.yaml) that names every file column exactly once.
  • decimal-not-float: Scores and indicators are decimal(38,20), parsed with Python Decimal from the file text, rendered in fixed notation with 20 fractional digits in the CSV, the digest and SQL. A value that does not fit stops the build.
  • v2-no-route-code: The version 2 value -1 in eleven routed indicators and their deciles for S01010206 and S01010226 is kept as published and checked to occur nowhere else. Version 4's domain_e of exactly -1.0000 for S01008132 is an ordinary value.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• one-table-all-editions: One table, ahah_datazone, keyed by (ahah_version, datazone_code), one row per Scottish data zone per edition, with datazone_vintage. All five editions (1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1) are carried.
  • v5-1-names: Column names are those of the version 5.1 file. Earlier editions map onto them by an explicit per-edition mapping (mapping.yaml) that names every file column exactly once.
  • ranks-gb-only: Ranks, percentiles and deciles are stored as published, over Great Britain. No Scotland-only rank is computed.
  • percentile-scales: Indicator percentiles 0 to 100 and domain and index percentiles 1 to 100 are stored as published; an issue is logged with the authors (docs/PERCENTILES.md).

docs.text:
Indicator value as published. Units differ by edition: see the data dictionary.

Type: decimal (SQL Server decimal(38,20)). Nullable: yes. Group: indicators (raw values). Editions: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1.

docs.title: What it is, by edition
docs.text: Editions Definition Unit Source 1 Annual mean nitrogen dioxide concentration: DEFRA modelled estimates on a 1 km grid, averaged over the cells overlapping the area. Part of the physical environment domain in this edition. µg/m³ paraphrased from Daras K, Green MA, Davies A, Barr B, Singleton A (2019), Methods, air quality 2 Units unconfirmed: the version 2 documentation is not held. The column names suggest the revised method of version 3. unconfirmed our wording 3, 4, 5.1 “Annual mean Nitrogen Dioxide (ugm3)” µg/m³ quoted from AHAH version 5 variable dictionary, row NO2 3, 4, 5.1 The version 5 wording; the version 3 and 4 methods are the same drive-time or raster approach (methodology report, sections 3 and 5), and version 4 publishes values to 4 decimals. our wording

docs.title: PM10
docs.text:
Indicator value as published. Units differ by edition: see the data dictionary.

Type: decimal (SQL Server decimal(38,20)). Nullable: yes. Group: indicators (raw values). Editions: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1.

docs.title: What it is, by edition
docs.text: Editions Definition Unit Source 1 Annual mean particulate matter, PM10 concentration: DEFRA modelled estimates on a 1 km grid, averaged over the cells overlapping the area. Part of the physical environment domain in this edition. µg/m³ paraphrased from Daras K, Green MA, Davies A, Barr B, Singleton A (2019), Methods, air quality 2 Units unconfirmed: the version 2 documentation is not held. The column names suggest the revised method of version 3. unconfirmed our wording 3, 4, 5.1 “Annual mean Particulate Matter (ugm3)” µg/m³ quoted from AHAH version 5 variable dictionary, row PM10 3, 4, 5.1 The version 5 wording; the version 3 and 4 methods are the same drive-time or raster approach (methodology report, sections 3 and 5), and version 4 publishes values to 4 decimals. our wording

• one-table-all-editions: One table, ahah_datazone, keyed by (ahah_version, datazone_code), one row per Scottish data zone per edition, with datazone_vintage. All five editions (1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1) are carried.
  • v5-1-names: Column names are those of the version 5.1 file. Earlier editions map onto them by an explicit per-edition mapping (mapping.yaml) that names every file column exactly once.
  • ranks-gb-only: Ranks, percentiles and deciles are stored as published, over Great Britain. No Scotland-only rank is computed.

docs.title: domain_e_exp
docs.text:
Domain score of editions 1 and 2: the exponentially transformed domain rank, 0 to 100, 100 is the worst rank. Not the probit scale of the later editions.

Type: decimal (SQL Server decimal(38,20)). Nullable: yes. Group: domain scores (exponential, editions 1 and 2). Editions: 1, 2; NULL in 3, 4, 5.1.

docs.title: What it is, by edition
docs.text: Editions Definition Unit Source 1 The physical environment domain score of edition 1, combining green space with the NO2, PM10 and SO2 indicators with equal weights (Daras et al. 2019, pages 3 to 5): the exponentially transformed domain rank, 0 to 100, 100 the worst rank. From edition 3 this column is an air quality domain without green space. 0 to 100 paraphrased from Daras K, Green MA, Davies A, Barr B, Singleton A (2019), pages 3 to 5, physical environment domain 2 The exponentially transformed domain rank, 0 to 100, 100 the worst rank, as in edition 1; which indicators edition 2 combines is unconfirmed (its documentation is not held). It inverts exactly to an integer rank, so it is not the probit scale of the later editions. 0 to 100 our wording, decision v1-v2-exponential-domains

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• one-table-all-editions: One table, ahah_datazone, keyed by (ahah_version, datazone_code), one row per Scottish data zone per edition, with datazone_vintage. All five editions (1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1) are carried.
  • v5-1-names: Column names are those of the version 5.1 file. Earlier editions map onto them by an explicit per-edition mapping (mapping.yaml) that names every file column exactly once.
  • ranks-gb-only: Ranks, percentiles and deciles are stored as published, over Great Britain. No Scotland-only rank is computed.
  • percentile-scales: Indicator percentiles 0 to 100 and domain and index percentiles 1 to 100 are stored as published; an issue is logged with the authors (docs/PERCENTILES.md).

docs.title: datazone-lists
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-29.

Decision. The 2011 and 2022 data zone lookups from data.gov.scot are pinned as reference lists, independent of any postcode product. Every zone of a vintage must appear exactly once in every edition of that vintage.

Why. postcode-simd pins no standalone list.

Columns (2): datazone_code, datazone_vintage

docs.title: decimal-not-float
docs.text:
Date: 2026-10-29.

Decision. Scores and indicators are decimal(38,20), parsed with Python Decimal from the file text, rendered in fixed notation with 20 fractional digits in the CSV, the digest and SQL. A value that does not fit stops the build.

Why. Files carry up to 20 fractional digits and version 3 uses scientific notation; a float would alter them.
